doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: The most ridiculous gigs: a cut-up show revival and the circus
summary: Gallodoro describes a recent show revival with chaotic page cuts, contrasts the circus and carnival work, and passes on tips about waltz tempos.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Yeah. You have to have it I think to be in the music business. This is always a hard question but I’ll ask it anyway. Can you think of a gig that was so ridiculous that you did. Because you mentioned the circus you know. And I know, did you ever find yourself doing a gig that you said, “I can’t believe that I’m doing this.”
Son of a gun, I just played one.

But I’m not going to mention the show, nor the conductor, because the conductor was great. We just did a revival of a famous show. And I never in my life saw cut to here, cut back to here, then cut way over here, then cut back. You couldn’t possibly come in on time and turn the pages. And absolutely unbelievable. I’ve played shows, yeah, you’d make a cut here, you’d play and then you wait and then a cut here. But this was back and forth, back and forth, back and forth. Hideous. That was the worst, the toughest. And yet the music was not hard to play. No there was nothing impossible to play. But the cuts going back and forth. They didn’t bother to make photostats and so forth. Now the circus, the circus was nothing, everything was marked. But the only thing about the circus, it’s loud and louder. You never can play soft. And fast. Well now sometimes when you play a waltz. If you’re playing a waltz, now this is something that I try to teach — instantly © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

you’ve got to go fast. Say you’re playing a waltz for the trapeze [humms] Right then, simultaneously, not variable. But that’s good experience. The carnival was a great experience. Oh my goodness. Four and a half years of that. [inaudible] had to play behind singers.
But I didn’t mention the show, right?
You didn’t mention the show, we don’t know who the conductor was. We know what it must have looked like, like they cut all the music up and put it back together.
He had his hands full. You know what he said then? He says, “Look guys, do the best you can.” But the best you can is not good enough.
